title: Babies Are Freezing to Death in Gaza. Israeli Policy and the World’s Inaction Are to Blame
author: Dr. Thaer Ahmad
content:

media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fbfb472ac-0113-4eb2-a114-4086b16f86e7_4812x3282.jpeg)_A
relative of the 1-month-old Saeed Abdeen, who died of hypothermia, carries his
body to the cemetery before burying him in Khan Younis, Gaza, on Dec. 18,
2025. Photo by Abdallah F.s. Alattar/Anadolu via Getty Images_

The images and testimonies emerging from Gaza this winter are tragic and
unbearable. A 2-week‑old infant, Mohammed Khalil, was found "[cold as
ice](https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2025/12/18/baby-mohammed-freezes-to-
death-as-gaza-battles-winter-and-displacement)" in a tent flooded by days of
heavy rain. A 29‑day‑old premature baby, Saeed Abdeen, [died from
hypothermia](https://apnews.com/article/gaza-hypothermia-winter-
infant-759f79812968d06fa82f1c85e0455861) despite desperate attempts by his
family to keep him warm in their falling-apart nylon tent. Families waking
each morning to water [flooding their
bedding](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2025/12/utterly-preventable-
gaza-flood-tragedy-must-mobilize-action-to-end-israels-genocide/) from
underneath, unable to dry anything in the relentless damp.

This is not simply the consequence of a harsh winter and the elements. These
are the predictable and preventable outcomes of a suffocating siege and
systematic obstruction of aid that have stripped more than two million
Palestinians of the minimum conditions required for human survival. Storm
Byron may have brought the rain and freezing temperatures, but Israeli policy
is what is killing children.

Over recent days, [at least 16 deaths](https://www.newarab.com/news/gaza-
storm-byron-kills-least-16-including-children) have been reported amid heavy
rains and plunging temperatures. [Waterlogged
buildings](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/five-said-killed-in-
house-collapse-in-northern-gazas-beit-lahiya/) collapsed on families who had
no safer shelter, and [three children were
killed](https://www.haaretz.com/gaza/2025-12-12/ty-article/.premium/in-gaza-
and-israel-storm-byron-ravages-buildings-and-tents-several-dead-from-
hypothermia/0000019b-1244-dda6-a7fb-3645bd310000) as the storm raged over
displacement camps and makeshift tents atop rubble. [More than 79,000
people](https://www.unrwa.org/resources/reports/unrwa-situation-
report-201-situation-gaza-strip-and-west-bank-including-east-jerusalem) are
crowded into over 100 UNRWA schools turned into shelters, each one more
damaged than the other, overrun with overflowing sewage from the rainfall.
Humanitarian teams are attempting to address the issues on the ground in real
time, but the most basic supplies needed, like timber, plywood, warm clothes,
and proper tents, [continue to sit idly at
crossings](https://www.timesofisrael.com/un-gaza-bound-shelter-materials-
refused-entry-leaving-displaced-masses-exposed/) as they are blocked by
Israeli authorities.

The deadly cold fell on a population already
[debilitated](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/10/7/two-years-of-israels-
genocide-in-gaza-by-the-numbers) by more than two years of relentless and
indiscriminate bombardment, multiple forced displacements, and the collapse of
Gaza's healthcare system. Since the so-called "ceasefire" began on Oct. 10, we
have repeatedly heard the international community call for a ["scaling up of
aid."](https://www.ifrc.org/article/ifrc-statement-humanitarian-aid-gaza-we-
must-seize-crucial-moment-gazas-people) But the reality on the ground shows
that the [agreed-upon 600
trucks](https://www.imeupolicyproject.org/memos/next-phase-of-trumps-gaza-
plan-raises-concerns-about-gazas-partition-palestinian-freedom) of
humanitarian aid per day (outlined in President Donald Trump's proposal) has
yet to materialize. Instead, the average has been a fraction of that, around
244 trucks a day, according to Palestinian authorities.

Children are dying for lack of what any parent would call the bare
necessities: blankets, tents, shoes, soap. More than [27,000 tents have been
flooded](https://erccportal.jrc.ec.europa.eu/ECHO-Products/Echo-Flash#/echo-
flash-items/30148), blown away, or ripped apart. Some [13,000
families](https://www.ochaopt.org/content/gaza-humanitarian-response-
situation-report-no-22) are once again out on the street. OCHA
[estimates](https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/un-agency-warns-
displaced-gazans-face-floods-emergency-supplies-blocked-2025-12-12/) 795,000
people are in immediate danger amidst the freezing rain and plunging
temperatures. And because construction materials are still restricted by
Israel as so‑called "[dual‑use](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/gaza/torrential-
rain-death-destruction-war-battered-gaza-rcna248824)" items, families have no
way to reinforce their shelters. Even [sandbags and water
pumps](https://www.iom.int/news/nearly-795000-displaced-palestinians-flood-
risk-after-storm-byron-makes-landfall-gaza) sit blocked at the border.

Israel's restrictions have also forced the closure of child‑friendly spaces
and psychosocial centers. Save the Children [shut down four of its
sites](https://www.savethechildren.org/us/about-us/media-and-news/2025-press-
releases/gaza-storms-israeli-government-aid-restrictions) due to flooding and
sewage intrusion. And even if the children had access to these spaces of
reprieve, they still lacked the shoes, coats, or safety to be able to trek
through the sludge and mud that enveloped the camp's dirt roads.

post-
media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fb403b88e-19ad-4e12-8d34-edc93f001664_5760x3840.jpeg)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!GWif!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-
post-
media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fb403b88e-19ad-4e12-8d34-edc93f001664_5760x3840.jpeg)_Palestinians
struggle to survive in makeshift tents amid harsh winter conditions and the
heavy toll of Israeli attacks in Deir al Balah, Gaza, on Dec. 20, 2025. Photo
by Anadolu via Getty Images_

The cruelty of these conditions is tragically unthinkable. Families huddle
around their infants at night. Mothers and fathers lie awake, checking whether
their children are still breathing. The small bodies of infants are unable to
generate enough heat to regulate their temperatures and not enough meat on
their bones to insulate them further from the bitter cold. Healthy and full-
term newborn babies are susceptible to complications caused by hypothermia,
but in Gaza, many newborns are born prematurely with low birth weight and to
mothers having difficulty nursing, confined to an ever-shrinking Gaza with no
electricity, no sanitation, and no materials to rebuild. Respiratory
infections are [surging](https://prezly.msf.org.uk/msf-gaza-29-day-old-baby-
dies-from-hypothermia-at-nasser-hospital). Waterborne
[diseases](https://www.emro.who.int/media/news/risk-of-disease-spread-soars-
in-gaza-as-health-facilities-water-and-sanitation-systems-disrupted.html) are
rising. If a Palestinian newborn or infant miraculously survives the cold
night, they are still fighting for their life amidst communicable diseases and
a lack of access to proper healthcare. Even the most vigilant parents who
identify early signs of distress in their babies will find no ambulance or car
to be able to navigate the streets during the flooding, and hospitals without
warmers or supplies to revive them.

Despite the US brokered ceasefire, Israel has continued attacks that have
[killed hundreds of Palestinians](https://t.me/s/MOHMediaGaza) and injured
more than 1,000 since the agreement began. Homes are still being destroyed.
Aid requests are still being rejected. Doctors are still being denied entry,
including myself.

#### **The Blame Is Ours**

There is a thorough attempt to undermine the welfare of the Palestinian
population in Gaza via the blocking of humanitarian aid. The world must stop
treating the word "ceasefire" as a guarantee of safety when Gaza's residents
remain under fire, under siege, and under conditions that guarantee more
suffering and heartbreak.

Images of [mobile homes](https://www.egypttoday.com/Article/1/143069/Egypt-
prepares-machinery-mobile-homes-to-aid-Gaza-reconstruction) in Egypt or Jordan
awaiting approval to enter Gaza only confirm what every humanitarian
organization has stated: if access doesn't change, more infants will die.
Pontificating over who will make up an "[international stabilization
force](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/us-aims-international-gaza-
force-deployment-early-next-year-say-us-officials-2025-12-12/)" underscores a
lack of seriousness by the international community. Parents are burying their
babies and can't find a piece of cloth to cover their surviving children; the
discussion should be solely focused on lifting the blockade and allowing aid
to enter without restrictions. If that happens, lives will be saved; it is as
simple as that.

It is not harsh weather that is killing Gaza's children. It is the intentional
effort by Israel to ensure that cold, heat, and humidity are made
unsurvivable. It is the willful betrayal of international humanitarian law,
reinforced by dehumanizing rhetoric amplified by governments and mainstream
media.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!aiik!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-
post-
media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fc9e9000e-7e07-457e-811d-b93151b360de_5157x3438.jpeg)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!aiik!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-
post-
media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fc9e9000e-7e07-457e-811d-b93151b360de_5157x3438.jpeg)_Palestinians
struggle to live under harsh conditions as cold weather damages tents amid
Israeli attacks in Gaza City on Dec. 12, 2025. Photo by Mahmoud Abu
Hamda/Anadolu via Getty Images_

As if a baby, less than a month old, dying from the cold is somehow less
tragic because they are Palestinian.

Are we foolish enough to believe that aid will miraculously enter without
accountability? When there are no consequences for starving a population,
cutting off water and electricity, and blocking access to shelter materials
and treatment, how can we not expect the death toll to rise?

We can blame the strong winds. We can blame the cruel winter. But the blame is
ours… unless policymakers and officials understand that we are not deceived by
phony ceasefires and false promises. The stakes remain high, the urgency is
extraordinary, and we must not fall into the trap of those who seek to
convince us otherwise.

_**Dr. Thaer Ahmad** is a Palestinian-American emergency room physician from
Chicago. He traveled to Gaza in 2024 with humanitarian aid organizations and
worked at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis and Al-Aqsa Hospital in Deir al-
Balah._
